name: the #general channel of the server, empty

regions_read.verdict_on_region: names the channel the user is in ('# general' in the top bar, with the '#' channel sign) — a place name, counted

names the server, but as the opening greeting of the channel's message history, not as a screen title; it sits in the scrolling message stream and moves up and away as soon as messages exist (seen live) — content, not counted as an identifier

initial_rationale: top bar '# general' with the '#' channel sign and back arrow names the channel; the mid-screen welcome is a greeting in the message stream

test_cases.precondition: app open on the #general channel of the server, composer empty
test_cases.action: scroll the message area down and up; then watch the mid-screen 'Welcome to Accessibility Testin's server' heading as a message is added to the channel
test_cases.expected_result: the heading either stays fixed as a screen title or moves with the message stream
test_cases.confirms_if: n/a for the screen verdict (the top bar decides it); the region is dismissed as content if it moves with the messages
test_cases.overturns_if: the heading is pinned in place like a title
test_cases.observed_result: top bar '# general' / '1 Online' stayed fixed through every scroll; the welcome heading is the first item of the message history — when a message was present it slid upward under the top bar and was partly hidden. It is a greeting in the content, not a title. (A GIF was accidentally posted during this test and was deleted straight after; the channel was restored to its captured empty state.)

deciding_evidence: tested live: top bar '# general' / '1 Online' stayed fixed through every scroll; the welcome heading is the first item of the message history — when a message was present it slid upward under the top bar and was partly hidden. It is a greeting in the content, not a title
